title: Borders Bear the Brunt: State Environmental Review and Severed Agglomerations
abstract: We study how state environmental review laws (SEPAs) shape local business activity. Using a stacked, border-pair event design around staggered SEPAs, we compare adjacent counties on either side of state lines. SEPA-side border counties experience slower post-adoption growth that cumulates into persistent level losses over two decades, with no mirror-image gains across the border and no broad underperformance in state interiors. Effects are strongest for SEPA-treated counties that border large metro areas, when SEPAs have substantive provisions, and when states devote more resources to environmental protection, and they fall disproportionately on pollution-intensive sectors and small firms. In sum, local environmental regulations can erode local agglomerations, adversely affecting local small business growth.
abstract_zh: 我们研究州环境审查法（SEPA）如何影响地方商业活动。利用围绕交错实施的SEPA构建的堆叠式边界配对事件设计，我们比较了州界两侧相邻的县。实施SEPA一侧的边界县在政策实施后增长较慢，这种增长差距在二十年间累积为持续的水平损失；跨越边界的另一侧并未出现对称的收益，州内部也未出现广泛的表现不佳。在以下情形中效应最为显著：受SEPA影响的县毗邻大都市区、SEPA包含实质性条款，以及各州在环境保护方面投入更多资源。效应还不成比例地落在污染密集型行业和小企业身上。总之，地方环境法规可能侵蚀地方产业集聚，从而对地方小企业的增长产生不利影响。

Propagation of Climate Disasters through Ownership Networks
abstract: Institutional investors holding firms hit by climate-related disasters vote more in favor of climate-related shareholder proposals at their other portfolio firms. This relation arises via investors becoming more active voters on climate-related proposals and is strongest following recent exposure to large value-relevant disasters, during periods of elevated attention to climate risks, and for votes occurring at carbon-intensive firms. Aggregating to the firm level, firms with impacted investors exhibit lower climate change sentiment on conference calls and a longer-term decrease in emissions. Thus, climate disasters ripple through ownership networks to influence corporate behavior toward environmental responsibility.
abstract_zh: 持有遭受气候相关灾害冲击企业股份的机构投资者，在其其他投资组合企业中，会更多地投票支持气候相关的股东提案。这种关系源于投资者在气候相关提案上变得更加积极地投票；该效应在近期遭遇大规模、与价值相关的灾害之后最为强烈，在对气候风险关注度上升的时期最为明显，并且在碳密集型企业的投票中表现最突出。在企业层面汇总后，受影响投资者所持有的企业在电话会议中表现出的气候变化情绪较低，且排放量出现长期下降。因此，气候灾害通过所有权网络产生连锁反应，影响企业履行环境责任的行为。
